extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals (PRSA members and practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: The PRSA Code of Ethics sets core professional values and provisions of conduct for public relations practitioners and provides topic-specific positions and advisory guidance (e.g., social media, AI, paid influencers). It is intended to guide ethical decision-making and behavior across PR activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We serve the public interest by acting as responsible advocates for those we represent. We provide a voice in the marketplace of ideas, facts, and viewpoints to aid informed public debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should advance clients’ interests while keeping the public interest in mind; disclosure and transparent representation of viewpoint/sponsor are implied as part of responsible advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We adhere to the highest standards of accuracy and truth in advancing the interests of those we represent and in communicating with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest and accurate in all communications; act promptly to correct erroneous communications for which the practitioner is responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We acquire and responsibly use specialized knowledge and experience. We advance the profession through continued professional development, research, and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain continued professional development, build credibility and relationships, and apply expertise responsibly in service of clients and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide objective counsel to those we represent. We are accountable for our actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid actions that compromise objectivity; be prepared to provide candid, independent counsel even when it conflicts with client preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are faithful to those we represent, while honoring our obligation to serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance obligations to clients/employers with duties to the public; do not sacrifice public interest for client loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We deal fairly with clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, the media, and the general public. We respect all opinions and support the right of free expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice equitable treatment of stakeholders and respect for differing views; support fair competition and intellectual property rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Flow of Information (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Protecting and advancing the free flow of accurate and truthful information is essential to serving the public interest and contributing to informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: maintain integrity of relationships with media, government officials and the public; aid informed decision-making. Guidelines: preserve the integrity of communication processes; be honest and accurate; act promptly to correct erroneous communications; ensure gifts are nominal, legal, and infrequent so as not to impede free flow. Examples of improper conduct: giving expensive gifts to influence coverage; entertaining government officials beyond legal limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Promoting healthy and fair competition among professionals preserves an ethical climate while fostering a robust business environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: promote respect and fair competition and widest practitioner choice. Guidelines: follow ethical hiring practices that respect open competition; preserve intellectual property rights. Examples of improper conduct: sharing privileged competitive information; spreading malicious rumors to recruit clients/employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Open communication fosters informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: build trust by revealing information needed for responsible decision-making. Guidelines: be honest and accurate; correct errors promptly; investigate truthfulness of released information; reveal sponsors and financial interests; avoid deceptive practices. Examples: creating front groups, lying by omission (failing to release financial info), failing to correct inaccurate website/media-kit info, employing people to pose as volunteers in ‘grassroots’ campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Client trust requires appropriate protection of confidential and private information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: protect privacy rights of clients, organizations, and individuals. Guidelines: safeguard confidences of present, former and prospective clients/employees; protect privileged, confidential, or insider information; advise appropriate authority if you discover confidential info is being divulged. Examples: taking confidential information to a new job and using it; intentionally leaking proprietary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Avoiding real, potential or perceived conflicts of interest builds the trust of clients, employers, and the publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: earn trust and mutual respect. Guidelines: act in best interests of client/employer even if it subordinates personal interests; avoid actions that may appear to compromise judgement; disclose promptly any existing or potential conflicts to affected parties; encourage clients to determine if a conflict exists after notification. Examples: failing to disclose a financial interest in a client’s competitor; representing a competitor without informing a prospective client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Public relations professionals work constantly to strengthen the public’s trust in the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: build respect and credibility for the profession and improve practices. Guidelines: acknowledge obligation to protect and enhance the profession; keep informed and pursue professional development; decline representation that contradicts the Code; accurately define what PR can accomplish; counsel and require subordinates to adhere to ethical decision making; report noncompliant practices. Examples: publicly declaring a product safe without disclosing contrary evidence; assigning questionable client work to non-members to avoid obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs) (mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS issues Ethical Standards Advisories to provide guidance within the framework of the Code as issues arise; ESAs are informational and not legal advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESAs (e.g., ESA on misinformation) provide topic-specific clarifying guidance and are available to members (many on MyPRSA). They are used to interpret and apply Code provisions to emerging issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay-for-Play (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: paying for development/publishing of content (print or digital) that results in undisclosed placement or exposure; pay-for-play deceives consumers by implying earned third‑party credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: pay-for-play conflicts with Code provisions (Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession). Recommendations: request and include disclosure when compensation provided for exposure; encourage disclosure of travel/lodging/gifts given to media/digital influencers; always encourage clear disclosure of material information consumers should have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics & Social Media (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media’s speed and reach raise ethical responsibilities; practitioners must adhere to the PRSA Code when using social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant provisions: Disclosure of Information, Safeguarding Confidences, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: disclose paid placements and associations; protect confidential information and be mindful of inadvertent disclosures; respect employee free speech per NLRB guidance; disclose conflicts of interest and require proper influencer disclosures per FTC; ensure gifts are nominal/legal/infrequent; use social platforms to inform and share best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is unauthorized use or close imitation of another’s language/ideas and representing them as one’s own; inadvertent plagiarism carries equal weight with intentional misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must respect intellectual property and attribution rules. Recommendations: do not copy content even if edited; use own words and paraphrase with attribution; when quoting exact wording use quotation marks and credit the source; disclose all sources; obtain permissions or pay licensing when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid Spokespersons and Influencers (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone paid to serve as a spokesperson, advocate or influencer must disclose the contractual arrangement or relationship with the compensating interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant provisions: Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: disclose commercial relationships in advance or simultaneously in the same forum; all parties in the contract must disclose; be honest and accurate in communications and reveal sponsors and financial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing Front Groups (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A front group is created or labeled to mislead the public about its true mission; assisting front groups is deceptive and violates the Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant provisions: Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: avoid assisting or creating front groups even if legal; uphold transparency and avoid deceptive descriptions of goals, sponsors, tactics or participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating Fees or Compensation (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging clients for services not performed, inflating fees, or misrepresenting services harms the profession and is unethical (and sometimes illegal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant provision: Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: charge only for services rendered per contracts; properly report services rendered, time spent, out-of-pocket charges and support data; avoid inflating charges or related support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Advertising & Sponsored Content (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a clear distinction between organic content and sponsored/native advertising; the sponsor should be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant provisions: Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Competition, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: ensure sponsorship is fully disclosed and consistently clear to consumers; disclosures should be appropriate to the medium, easily identifiable, and not attempt to deceive consumers into thinking content is independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and Leadership Accountabilities (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: When machine learning/AI systems make decisions, accountability should rest with human beings with oversight responsibilities at the time the errant decision is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant provisions: Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: counsel senior leadership that machines cannot be held solely accountable; draw clear lines of human responsibility; assign oversight ownership; present human accountability clearly in communications; identify root causes and corrective actions with transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media as a Reflection of Majority Opinion (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media activity is not a scientifically vetted indicator of majority public opinion and may be driven by a small, highly active minority of users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant provisions: Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: when presenting analysis based on social media, remind audiences the platform is informal and may not represent general public sentiment; contextualize insights and avoid overstating representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Leaks (position & guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members should refrain from leaking information to media or stakeholders without organizational approval; leaking undermines trust and may be illegal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant provisions: Safeguarding Confidences, Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: be aware of laws, regulations, contracts (NDAs) and standing procedures governing disclosure; adhere to contractual and legal obligations; never autonomously share confidential information; follow approval procedures for disclosures.
